tldr: PAE is a learning system that enables foundation model agents to autonomously discover and practice skills through a context-aware task proposer, agent policy, and VLM-based evaluator in an online RL loop, achieving significant zero-shot generalization gains on web navigation benchmarks.
contributions: Proposed PAE (Proposer-Agent-Evaluator), the first effective learning system applying autonomous task proposal with RL for internet agents that generalizes to real-world human-annotated benchmarks
Introduced a context-aware task proposer that generates feasible tasks using environment context such as user demos or website names alone
Designed an image-based outcome evaluator that provides robust sparse 0/1 rewards without accessing hidden state information
Incorporated a chain-of-thought reasoning step before actual web actions to improve generalization to unseen human requests
Demonstrated that agents can autonomously discover useful skills even when the task proposer and evaluator are significantly worse than the agent model
methods: PAE operates as a context-aware Markov Decision Process where a VLM-based task proposer generates tasks conditioned on environment context (e.g., website names or user demo screenshots), an agent policy attempts these tasks with chain-of-thought reasoning followed by grounded web operations, and an image-based evaluator assesses success from the final three screenshots and agent answers to produce 0/1 reward signals. The agent policy is trained via Filtered Behavior Cloning, which imitates thoughts and actions from successful trajectories with negative log-likelihood loss, using a simple online policy optimization approach. The system was evaluated on vision-based web navigation across real-world websites (Amazon) from WebVoyager and self-hosted websites from WebArena.
results: PAE with LLaVa-1.6 (7B) achieves a 30% relative improvement in average success rate compared to the baseline, enabling it to reach performance comparable to LLaVa-1.6-34B fine-tuned with demonstration data despite using 5x fewer test-time compute. Against state-of-the-art open-source VLM agents including Qwen2VL-72B, PAE achieves an absolute performance gain of over 10% (from 22.6% to 33.0%). Experiments were conducted on WebVoyager and WebArena benchmarks spanning more than 100 domains.
limitations: The system relies on infrastructure complexity involving thousands of distributed fully-functioning web browsers
The evaluation results may differ from reported values in other papers due to the dynamic nature of online websites
Performance depends on the capability of the task proposer and evaluator models, though experiments show robustness even when they are worse than the agent
The study focuses specifically on vision-based web navigation agents, so generalization to other domains (e.g., physical robots) is not validated
